surfaces.label: Compiler
surfaces.current: Inline Pug and Jade cover elements, components, directives, slots, interpolation, build-time conditionals and iteration, mixins, attributes and relative includes; their rendered HTML twins compile identically in DOM, SSR and Vapor, with authored diagnostics and source maps.
surfaces.remaining: Arbitrary executable JavaScript, while and case control flow, template inheritance, filters, rooted includes and external template src stay explicitly refused instead of entering the supported deterministic subset.

surfaces.label: Vite / bundlers
surfaces.current: Vite client and SSR, Rollup, webpack and Rspack render the supported Pug and Jade twins like HTML; relative include dependencies are watched and invalidate the owning SFC through a real Vite HMR graph.
surfaces.remaining: Bundlers inherit the compiler's deterministic-subset refusals; filtered, rooted or over-budget include graphs fail closed and do not produce partial modules.

witnesses.anchor: Pug include edits reach the owning module through the real Vite watcher

surfaces.label: Type checker
surfaces.current: Supported inline attribute, directive and interpolation expressions project through the same virtual TypeScript contract as their HTML twins; Pug and Jade report the same diagnostics at authored positions.
surfaces.remaining: External template src and deliberately refused Pug programs are not projected, because no supported template program exists from which to derive trustworthy TypeScript ranges.

surfaces.label: Linter
surfaces.current: All supported matrix programs lint like their rendered HTML twins and diagnostics map to authored Pug or Jade bytes. A pinned dho-web-client SFC is rendered with pug 3.0.4, then Patina and eslint-plugin-vue 10.9.2 must match the same rule, severity, count and upstream message prefix; Patina's full message separately pins its authored element context.
surfaces.remaining: Autofixes inside the derived template remain withheld. vue-eslint-parser cannot expose inside-Pug nodes, so upstream parity is measured against the exact rendered HTML twin while script findings remain directly comparable.

witnesses.anchor: the TypeScript runner keeps pug template findings out of the scored surface
a pinned dho Pug project measures eslint-plugin-vue parity through its HTML twin

surfaces.label: Formatter
surfaces.current: Pug and Jade use an idempotent opaque-template strategy: outer indentation is normalized while relative program indentation and content stay verbatim.
surfaces.remaining: There is no language-aware Pug printer; formatting intentionally does not rewrite Pug syntax.

surfaces.label: LSP
surfaces.current: Inline tag and prop completion, hover, definition, references and rename use authored Pug ranges for supported templates; Jade shares the same route with dedicated completion and navigation coverage.
surfaces.remaining: External template src and deliberately refused Pug programs do not expose a complete editor surface, matching the compiler and type-checker boundary.

realProjects.current: The Real Project Matrix runs compile, typecheck, lint and formatter checks over pinned Pug applications including dho-web-client, Wave UI, Splitpanes, Vue Cal, Vux and lx-music-desktop; LSP and SSR Pug observers are part of the same qualification workflow.
